sections.markdown:
## C2 — Confusables and KG hints: hill parking, freeways, lane changes and passing

FACT_ID: sec09-R01 | anchor: A01
With a curb, downhill means wheels toward the curb and uphill means wheels away from it; without a curb, the wheels go right either way. [A01]
Why it matters: group parking; difficulty three; confusable sec09-F02 vs sec09-F03 vs sec09-F04. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0017]

FACT_ID: sec09-R02 | anchor: A01
The rightmost freeway lane is for slower drivers, while the leftmost lane is reserved for passing, left turns and heavy-traffic situations. [A01]
Why it matters: group freeway; difficulty two; confusable sec09-F11 vs sec09-F12. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0017]

FACT_ID: sec09-R03 | anchor: A01
When entering a freeway you match its speed and yield to it; stopping in the acceleration lane is a last resort, except on a metered ramp where you stop for the signal. [A01]
Why it matters: group freeway; difficulty two; confusable sec09-F08 vs sec09-F09. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0017]

FACT_ID: sec09-R04 | anchor: A02
On the exit you keep your speed until inside the deceleration lane and slow down there, not on the freeway itself. [A02]
Why it matters: group freeway; difficulty two; prereq sec09-F16. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0018]

FACT_ID: sec09-R05 | anchor: A02
The lane-change signal runs at least 3 seconds or 200 feet before you move, and goes off within 3 seconds after you finish. [A02]
Why it matters: group lane change; difficulty two; prereq sec09-F20 and sec09-F21. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0018]

FACT_ID: sec09-R06 | anchor: A02
Mirrors are not enough for a lane change, because the blind spot just behind and beside you needs an over-the-shoulder look. [A02]
Why it matters: group lane change; difficulty one; prereq sec09-F19. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0018]

FACT_ID: sec09-R07 | anchor: A02
Passing on the right is allowed on one-way streets and roads with two or more lanes each way, but passing on the shoulder or off the pavement never is. [A02]
Why it matters: group passing; difficulty three; prereq sec09-F23. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0018]

FACT_ID: sec09-R08 | anchor: A02
Return to your lane after passing when you see both headlights of the passed vehicle in the rearview mirror, and finish before a solid yellow line begins. [A02]
Why it matters: group passing; difficulty two; prereq sec09-F25 and sec09-F31. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0018]

Misconception: you may merge onto the freeway anywhere along the ramp; wait until the solid white line ends. [A01]
Misconception: the left lane is a fast cruising lane; it is reserved for passing, left turns and heavy traffic. [A01]
Misconception: slowing down before reaching the deceleration lane is safest; hold your speed until you are in it. [A02]
Misconception: you may never cross a solid yellow line to pass; a brief crossing is allowed to pass a bicyclist when the way ahead is clear. [A02]
Mnemonic: Up and away, down toward the curb, no curb turn right. [A01]
Mnemonic: Signal, mirror, shoulder, move. [A02]
Glossary: Acceleration lane means the ramp lane used to build speed before merging onto a freeway. [A01]
Glossary: Metered ramp means an entrance ramp with a signal that releases vehicles onto the freeway. [A01]
Glossary: Deceleration lane means the lane used to slow down before reaching a freeway exit ramp. [A02]
Glossary: Blind spot means the area beside and behind your vehicle that your mirrors do not show. [A02]
